Let
\[
x=\sum_{\omega\in S_5}2^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}\omega\in \mathbb C[S_5].
\]
Then the matrix \(A\) is the matrix of the right-regular operator
\[
R(1+x):e_\sigma\mapsto e_\sigma+\sum_{\omega}2^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}e_{\sigma\omega}.
\]
For each irreducible representation \(\rho_\lambda\) of \(S_5\), indexed by partitions \(\lambda\vdash 5\), the regular representation contains \(\dim\rho_\lambda\) copies of \(\rho_\lambda\). Hence
\[
\det A=\prod_{\lambda\vdash 5}\det\!\left(I_{\dim\lambda}+\sum_{\omega\in S_5}2^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}\rho_\lambda(\omega)\right)^{\dim\lambda}.
\]

Using the standard Specht-module models for the seven partitions of \(5\), the needed small determinants are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\lambda & \dim \lambda &
\det\!\left(I+\sum_{\omega}2^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}\rho_\lambda(\omega)\right)\\
\hline
(5)&1&9766\\
(4,1)&4&7825821652720\\
(3,2)&5&150086072221696\\
(3,1,1)&6&35829388145340160\\
(2,2,1)&5&6098985750016\\
(2,1,1,1)&4&5372345584\\
(1,1,1,1,1)&1&166
\end{array}
\]

For example, the two one-dimensional checks are
\[
1+\sum_{\omega}2^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}
=1+\prod_{k=1}^5(1+2+\cdots+2^{k-1})
=1+9765=9766,
\]
and
\[
1+\sum_{\omega}(-2)^{\operatorname{inv}(\omega)}
=1+\prod_{k=1}^5(1-2+\cdots+(-2)^{k-1})
=1+165=166.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\det A
=
9766\cdot
7825821652720^4\cdot
150086072221696^5\cdot
35829388145340160^6\cdot
6098985750016^5\cdot
5372345584^4\cdot
166
}.
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
\det A=

}.
\]
